newsitem.title: USA: TCF Financial to buy Standard Financial.
newsitem.headline: TCF Financial to buy Standard Financial.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp and Standard Financial Inc said Monday they signed a definitive merger agreement, under which TCF would acquire Standard Financial in a $424 million deal.
Based on the TCF closing price on March 14 of 44-5/8, the deal is valued at about $25 per Standard common share. Standard shares closed March 14 at 21-1/8.

The merger, in which TCF would be the surviving corporation, would create a company with $10 billion in assets and 276 financial services offices and more than 900 automatic teller machines (ATMs) in five Midwest states.
"We believe this merger will produce long-term revenue enhancements and meaningful cost savings," TCF Chairman William Cooper said in a statement.
The companies said the deal would be structured as a cash election merger, in which Standard stockholders would have the right to choose either cash or TCF common stock or a combination of the two.

Between 40 percent and 60 percent of the purchase would be paid in shares of TCF common stock, and the remainder would be paid in cash. The deal would be tax free for Standard stockholders to the extent that they received TCF stock.
TCF said it expects the merger would add to both reported and cash earnings in 1998.

The exchange ratio for shares of Standard stock would depend on the average trading price of TCF stock during the 30 trading days before the merger. If the average price of TCF stock were between $43.75 and $47.75, each Standard share would be converted into the right to receive between $24.69 and $25.81 per share. If the price of TCF stock were below $43.75 but greater than or equal to $37.50, each Standard share will be exchanged for an aggregate value of $24.69.
If the price of TCF stock were above $47.75 but less than or equal to $54, each Standard share would be exchanged for an aggregate of $25.81.

The definitive agreement was signed after completion of due diligence and approval of both companies' boards. It is subject to approval by Standard's stockholders and required regulatory filings and approvals.

The merger is expected to close in the third quarter of 1997 and be accounted for as a purchase transaction, the companies said. Standard has agreed to pay a $15 million termination fee if the merger agreement were terminated under certain circumstances.
In connection with the deal, TCF said it would record "intangibles" of about $200 million.
Standard said it postponed its annual meeting and plans to call a special meeting to seek stockholder approval of the merger.

Standard is a thrift institution with $2.4 billion in assets and 14 full service offices on the southwest side of Chicago and in the nearby southwestern and western suburbs. TCF is a bank holding company with $7.1 billion in assets and more than 260 financial services offices.
